questiontext.text:
Find the intervals of continuity of \(f \displaystyle (x) = {@fx@}\).

Note: To enter intervals of of continuity, you should write the relevant text in the table below.

Intervals Input Syntax
\( [a,b] \) cc(a,b)
\( (a,b) \) oo(a,b)
\( [a,b) \) co(a,b)
\( (a,b] \) oc(a,b)
\( (a, \infty) \) oo(a,inf)
\( (-\infty, b] \) oc(-inf,b)
\( (-\infty, \infty) \) oo(-inf,inf)

Note: For instance, the operators \( \cap \) and \( \cup \) will be typed like and, or respectively

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the intervals of continuity for the function \( \displaystyle f(x) = \sqrt{x^2 - {@aa@}}\), we need to consider where the function is defined and where it might have any discontinuities.

The function \(x \mapsto \displaystyle \sqrt{x^2 - {@aa@}}\) is defined on the interval satisfying \(x^2 - {@aa@} \geq 0\).

\( \displaystyle \begin{align} x^2 - {@aa@} & \geq 0 \\ x^2 & \geq {@aa@} \\ |x| & \geq {@sqrt(aa)@} \end{align} \)

We recall that \( \displaystyle |x| \geq r \, (r \in \mathbb{R}^+) \Leftrightarrow x \in {@oc(-inf,-r)@} \cup {@co(r,inf)@}\). Thus, \(f\) is defined on \({@oc(-inf,-sqrt(aa))@} \cup {@co(sqrt(aa),inf)@}\).

Since \(f\) is continuous on \({@oo(-inf,-sqrt(aa))@} \cup {@oo(sqrt(aa),inf)@}\) and \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \rightarrow{@-sqrt(aa)@}^{-}}f(x) = f({@-sqrt(aa)@})\) and \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \rightarrow{@sqrt(aa)@}^{+}}f(x) = f({@sqrt(aa)@})\).

Therefore, the function \( \displaystyle f \) is continuous on the interval \({@oc(-inf,-sqrt(aa))@} \cup {@co(sqrt(aa),inf)@}\).
